title: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife

reports.title: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife

summary:
Former Costa Mesa police officer Robert Jay Josett, 35, pleaded guilty to three misdemeanors after harassing a former mistress and misusing police databases. After she ended the relationship in April 2024, he contacted her thousands of times over nine months, sometimes more than 100 times in one day, and called her and her new boyfriend up to 58 times in a single day. He made 13 unauthorized searches in a state law enforcement database on her, a romantic rival, and his wife, and used a license plate reader system to track vehicles, even after being placed on leave.

He was served with a restraining order and termination notice on June 28, 2024, then drove by her home and was arrested. Josett was sentenced to three years informal probation and a 52-week domestic violence program, after spending nine months on a GPS ankle monitor. His law enforcement certification review by POST is pending.
